transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

Yeah, hey, thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes on my sales reports at work. Like, I'll be copying numbers over from the team dashboard—which, by the way, corporate just updated the software for that last week and it is a complete disaster. They changed the whole interface so now everything is buried under like three different menus, and my guys are complaining about it constantly. Jim, one of my senior reps, he actually threatened to go back to pen and paper, which is hilarious because his handwriting is terrible. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll copy the wrong numbers down, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. And the crazy thing is, I swear I went over it. I'll look right at the screen, think I checked it all, and still mess it up. It’s kind of like when I was trying to put together this gas grill over the weekend and I ended up with all these extra screws, even though I read the manual twice. My wife was pretty mad because we were supposed to have people over for burgers, but... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the reports. Yeah, I just keep missing things I shouldn't be missing.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted or having trouble focusing, not just at work but in other parts of your life as well?

Yeah, absolutely. It's like, when I'm trying to review call notes or look at the numbers, just one conversation across the room is all it takes. Or even a random thought about something at home, and suddenly I'm completely pulled off track before I even realize it. Speaking of home, my neighbor just bought this massive riding lawnmower, which is ridiculous because his yard is maybe a quarter of an acre, tops. I was looking out the window the other day while I was supposed to be paying the electric bill, and I just watched him do these tiny little laps. It took him longer to get the thing out of his shed than it did to cut the grass. And then I ended up looking up lawnmower prices online for like an hour. But yeah, if I'm at the office and someone even walks by my desk, my brain just follows them instead of whatever I'm supposed to be doing.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?

No, not really. I don't feel down or anything. I still like doing all my normal stuff. Like, I'm huge into fantasy football, and I'm definitely not losing interest in that. Actually, our draft was just last weekend and my buddy Mike, he drafted a kicker in the fourth round. The fourth round! I mean, who does that? He claimed it was an accident because he dropped his phone, but we all know he just panicked because all the good running backs were gone. We gave him so much grief for it. 

We usually order wings from this place down the street for the draft party, but they changed their sauce recipe recently and it's just not the same anymore. It's way too sweet now, you know? Like they dumped a whole bottle of honey in the buffalo sauce. I don't get why places mess with a good thing once they have it figured out. But, um... wait, what did you ask me originally? Oh, right, feeling hopeless. No, no, I feel fine mood-wise. I'm just frustrated with messing up my reports at work, that's all.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level, or do you ever feel like you're moving slower or talking slower than usual, or maybe feel more tired than normal even after getting enough rest?

Nah, I wouldn't say that. I definitely don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or talking slower or anything like that. My energy is pretty much the same as always. I mean, I drink my fair share of coffee, but who doesn't, right? 

Actually, speaking of that, corporate just put in one of those fancy espresso machines in the breakroom last month—the kind that grinds the beans right in front of you and froths the milk. It's supposed to be this big "morale booster" for the sales floor, but honestly, it takes like five minutes to make one cup, so there's always a massive line. And Dave—he's one of my newer guys—he stands there and makes himself like three double shots a day. I told him he's gonna give himself a heart attack before he even hits his quarterly quota. Plus, the machine is so incredibly loud, it sounds like an airplane taking off. You can hear it all the way down the hall while I'm trying to do my one-on-ones with the team, and it's super annoying. 

But, uh... man, I completely lost my train of thought. What were we talking about? Something about being tired?
Have you ever found that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in your usual activities, even things like fantasy football or spending time with friends?

No, like I said, I still love all that stuff. Fantasy football is great, hanging out with friends is great. We actually have this group text going right now where we're trying to figure out if we want to do a destination draft next year. My buddy Mike—the kicker guy—he wants to go to Vegas, but honestly, Vegas in August is just miserable. You walk outside for two seconds and you're sweating through your shirt. 

I went to Vegas for a sales conference a couple years ago, and they put us up in this hotel that was practically a maze. I swear, it took me twenty minutes just to find the elevators from the lobby, and then another ten to find the convention center. And the carpet in those places? It's always these crazy, loud patterns that kind of make you dizzy if you stare at it too long. Someone told me once they design it that way on purpose so you don't look at the floor and you look at the slot machines instead. Which is wild, right? Like, the psychology of casino design is a whole thing. They don't even have clocks on the walls. 

But anyway... wait, did you just ask me the same question again? About not liking my hobbies? Yeah, no, I'm good on that front. Still into everything I normally do.
Have you been feeling like you're not good at things or feeling guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel guilty or like I'm a bad person or anything. I'm just annoyed with myself for messing up those reports at work. It's just stupid mistakes, you know? Like putting the wrong client code in the spreadsheet. 

Speaking of spreadsheets, they just updated our software at the office and it's a total nightmare. The new interface is completely different, and all the buttons are in the wrong places. They said it was supposed to streamline our workflow, but I swear it takes me twice as long to do anything now. And the training they gave us? A joke. It was this pre-recorded video of some guy just clicking around the screen, and he was talking so fast you couldn't even follow his cursor. Half the team didn't even watch the whole thing. I caught Dave playing a game on his phone during the training session. I should probably write him up for that, but honestly, I don't even know how to use the new HR portal to file a write-up yet. They changed that, too! It's like they want us to fail. 

They did the same thing with the parking lot last year. Repainted all the lines and completely changed the traffic flow, and for like a month, people were almost crashing into each other every morning. I had to lay on my horn at this one lady who was going the wrong way down the row... 

But, uh, anyway. Guilt? No, I don't sit around feeling guilty or worthless. Just frustrated with the work stuff.
